title: Canon Packet
description: Authored-story canon ingested from the writer's development assets (synopsis, treatment, outline, story bible, wayfinder map, canon atoms, pitch exports). This artifact is the authoritative story source for the authored-film pipeline: downstream stages ADAPT it, they never rewrite it. Locks are immutable within a production run — conflicts escalate to the writer, never resolve silently.

format.description: The delivery format of the authored work this production serves

path.description: Absolute or project-relative path to the source file as read

authority.description: canon = authoritative story truth (atoms, locked continuity); locked_decision = writer-ratified decisions (wayfinder resolved tickets, MAP Decisions so far); writing_document = the writer's development docs (synopsis/treatment/outline/story bible) — authoritative below locks, above groundwork; groundwork = evidence and research, never story authority; reference = tone/visual reference only

sha256.description: Content hash at ingest time — provenance for 'what exactly did production read'. Required: production must be able to prove what it read.

locks.description: Immutable story decisions. Every downstream stage treats these the way the checkpoint writer treats human_approval_default — binding, never re-judged.

id.description: Stable id, e.g. lock-001 or the atom filename stem

decision.description: The locked decision, in the writer's terms — quoted or faithfully compressed, never reinterpreted

evidence_ref.description: Signed-event hash or other evidence pointer when the source carries one (e.g. atom evidence field)

scope.description: What this lock governs: premise, ending, character, tone, structure, dialogue, world_rule

protected_lines.description: Dialogue or text the writer has protected. Reproduced VERBATIM in any script section that uses them — paraphrase is a canon violation.

context.description: Where in the story this line lives

never_write_as.description: The writer's 'never write them as' rule — a hard constraint on scripting and asset direction

visual_continuity_risks.description: From the AI production annex — what generation tends to get wrong about this character

reference_assets.description: Paths/URLs to visual references for generation consistency

comps.description: Reference works, with what each comp contributes (e.g. 'X is tone, Y is shape')

structure_source.description: Which document the beat structure came from (outline > treatment > synopsis precedence)

summary.description: What happens, in the writer's terms

turn.description: How this beat turns — the state change it causes

lock_refs.description: Lock ids that constrain this beat

ai_production_notes.description: Aggregated from the writing documents' AI production annexes ('AI Production Implications' / 'AI production annex' sections)

open_questions.description: Every [NEEDS DECISION] marker, unresolved wayfinder ticket in scope, and gap the ingest could not fill without inventing canon. Blocking questions stop the pipeline at the next gate until the writer answers.

id.description: Stable id, e.g. q-001. canon_ruling decisions reference this via question_id to resolve the question.

blocking.description: true = production cannot proceed past the next gate without the writer's answer. The checkpoint writer enforces this: no post-ingest stage completes while a blocking question is open and unruled.

status.description: resolved = answered before/at ingest. Questions answered later stay 'open' here and are released by a canon_ruling decision carrying this question's id.

resolution_ref.description: decision_id of the canon_ruling that resolved this question, when status=resolved

suggested_resolution.description: e.g. 'wayfinder ticket', 'answer at canon gate', 'producer ruling'

documents_declined.description: Files present but deliberately excluded, with why (e.g. sketches — disposable, not canon)
